chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah Al-Madainy, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'For the Muslim upon his brother, from the rights, is that he greets him when he meets him, and visits him when he is sick, and advises him when he is absent, and says the Name of Allah when he sneezes, saying: "The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, there is no associate for Him," and he says to him: "May Allah have mercy on you." So he answers him, saying to him: "May Allah guide you and rectify your affairs." And he answers him when he invites him, and follows him (his funeral) when he dies.'

key_terms.يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ: May Allah guide you (response to sneezing)
key_terms.يُسَمِّتَهُ: Says the Name of Allah (upon sneezing)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights of a Muslim upon his brother according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the comprehensive social contract between Muslims, framing these etiquette rules as binding rights (huquq) that strengthen communal bonds. The specific response to sneezing, invoking Allah as 'Lord of the Worlds' without partner, reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating monotheistic affirmation into daily interactions, while the sequence of rights—from greeting to funeral attendance—illustrates the holistic care expected in the Muslim community.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Al Qasim Bin Suelyman, from Jarrah Al Madainy who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the Muslim upon his brother, from the rights, is that he greets upon him when he meets him, and he consoles him when he is sick, and he advises for him when he is absent, and he should Name Allah<sup>azwj</sup> when he sneezes by saying, ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Lord<sup>azwj</sup> or the worlds, there being no associate for Him<sup>azwj</sup>’, and he should be saying to him, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> be Merciful to You’. So he would answer him saying to him, ‘May Allah Guide you and Correct your affairs’, and he should answer him when he invites him, and should follow him (his funeral) when he dies’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa’id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad’ini who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Of the rights of a Muslim on his brother (in belief) is that on meeting him he should offer him the greeting of peace, visit him when he is ill, look after his interests in his absence and respond to his sneezing. On sneezing one should say: “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds, who has no partner.” In response to sneezing one should say, “May Allah grant you favors.” The sneezing person should reply back by saying, “May Allah guide you, and look after your concerns.” Of such rights is to accept his invitation and attend his funeral.’”
